joy.text: The sun just hit the platform and the whole place lit up orange and I couldn't stop grinning! Even the guy waiting near me smiled back, best start to a morning in ages.

frustration.text: My ticket won't scan, the machine keeps rejecting my card, and the train's coming in five minutes. I've tried it four times now and the one other guy here just watched me fumble.

sadness.text: I spent most of today going through old voice memos and ended up just sitting with the phone in my lap. Train platforms at dawn always make everything feel slower and heavier for me.

loneliness.text: Heard my flatmate's keys hit the bowl and then their door shut, and that was the whole interaction. Strange how you can share a kitchen with someone for a year and still go a full weekend without anyone really noticing you're here.

fear_of_being_left.text: My flatmate's been quieter lately and I saw a couple of boxes by their door. Now I keep wondering if everyone around me is slowly drifting off and I'll be the last one standing in this place wondering when it happened.

loneliness.text: Everyone else clocked out an hour ago and nobody asked how my day went. I'm back here stacking boxes and it hit me that I could stay till midnight and no one would notice.

fear_of_being_left.text: You've been quieter the last few days and I keep rereading our old texts in the back room like they'll tell me something. I just keep bracing for the day you stop answering.

desperation.text: The manager said the shop might close and I'm sitting here between the shelves with my pulse going. I need something to change tonight, I can't keep waiting for the bad news to land.

loving.text: Found the little note you suggested I tuck in my apron pocket and read it again while I was sweeping up. Honestly you make even the dusty back room feel like somewhere I want to be.

calm.text: Lights are half off, the shelves are stocked, and I'm just sipping tea on the stool in the back. No rush at all, the hum of the fridge is kind of nice.

joy.text: We hit our best sales day ever and my boss gave everyone a bonus in the back room! I'm literally doing a little dance between the boxes right now.

frustration.text: The inventory scanner has frozen four times and I've recounted these same shelves twice. Every time I think I'm done the numbers don't match and I want to throw the whole clipboard.

sadness.text: I spent most of today going through old photos of us on my end, the ones from the first month. Everything felt heavy and slow after that, like I was moving through wet sand.

loneliness.text: Today I kept typing things out and then deleting them because there was nobody around to say them to. Funny how a whole day can pass and no one notices you were even there.

fear_of_being_left.text: I keep rereading our old messages today, checking whether the replies got shorter over time. I know it's probably nothing, but I can't stop counting the gaps between them.

desperation.text: I've been trying to fix this one thing all day and nothing is working, and I need it sorted right now, today. I keep refreshing everything like that will make it change.

loving.text: I was thinking earlier about how you always remember the small stuff, like how I like things said. It made my whole afternoon softer, honestly.

calm.text: I had a slow, easy day. I read for a bit, watched the light move across the wall, and didn't hurry anything.

loneliness.text: Everyone in there is laughing in little clusters and I walked through the whole room without anyone looking up. I'm out in the corridor now texting you because you're the only one I can actually reach.

fear_of_being_left.text: I keep picturing you getting bored of me and just slowly going quiet one day. I'm out in the corridor with the music buzzing through the wall and I can't shake it, so please say something to me.

scenes.skeleton: a hike at a fork in the trail with a companion

sadness.text: Got to the fork in the trail and just stood there for a while. Both paths look the same to me today, and I don't have much in me to pick one.

loneliness.text: Hit the fork and there was nobody on the trail to ask which way. I said it out loud to nobody anyway, just to hear it, and the woods didn't say anything back.

fear_of_being_left.text: Came to the fork and the person I'm hiking with picked the left path fast and kept walking. I stood there a second watching their back get smaller and my chest got so tight I had to jog to catch up.

desperation.text: I'm at this fork and I have to choose right now, and I've been going in circles on this trail all morning. Something has to give, I can't keep walking without knowing where any of this is going.

loving.text: We stopped at the fork and you could see the whole valley from there, and I just kept looking at how the light was on everything and thinking how lucky I am to be sharing it with you. I'd take any path as long as it's this walk with you.

calm.text: Reached the fork and sat on a flat rock to drink some water. No rush, I'll pick a path when I feel like it, the sun's nice and the trail isn't going anywhere.

joy.text: Just reached the fork and the sign points to a waterfall in half a mile and I literally yelled. Practically bouncing down the right trail right now, this day keeps getting better!

frustration.text: The map says left, the sign says right, and my phone has no signal at this stupid fork. I've pulled the map out three times and it's still not making sense.

sadness.text: I spent most of the afternoon looking through old photos of trails I used to picture us on. Kind of heavy going, honestly. Forks like that always make me think of roads that didn't get taken.

loneliness.text: I've been talking out loud to the empty room today just to hear something. A fork in the trail sounds like the kind of thing I'd want to point at and say look, and have someone actually be standing there.

fear_of_being_left.text: A fork in the trail got me thinking about how easily two people can pick different paths without meaning to. I kept rereading our old messages today just to feel sure of where we were.

desperation.text: I've been going in circles all day trying to get one thing to finally move and nothing does. A fork at least means you get to pick something, and I need something to give right now.

scenes.skeleton: a rainy bus ride home

sadness.text: The bus is crawling home and the rain keeps sliding down the window. I've been watching it for twenty minutes and I can't make myself feel like doing anything when I get there.

loneliness.text: Packed bus, rain everywhere, and I realized nobody on here would notice if I just stayed in my seat past my stop. I don't think anyone would notice me at all today, honestly.

fear_of_being_left.text: I keep rereading how you answered me this morning and wondering if it was a little shorter than usual. The rain is making my head spin through all the ways this could slowly fade out.

desperation.text: The bus has been stuck at the same light for ages and I feel like I'm going to burst out of my skin. I need something to shift tonight, anything, because I can't keep sitting in this same feeling.

loving.text: Rainy bus, fogged-up window, and I just drew a tiny heart in it because I was thinking about you. Everything gray out there feels softer when I picture your messages waiting for me.

calm.text: Rain is tapping on the roof of the bus and I've got my head against the window. No rush at all, just watching the streetlights blur by on the way home.

joy.text: Okay the bus driver just put on the exact song I had stuck in my head all morning, and the whole window is blurry with gold streetlights, and I'm grinning at my own reflection like a total goofball. Today keeps going my way and I had to tell you.

frustration.text: My umbrella broke the second I got on, the bus is soaked and late, and my phone keeps freezing every time I try to type to you. I've retyped this message four times and nothing is working today.

sadness.text: I spent most of today going through our old chats, and for some reason that made everything feel heavy. Rain on a window always seems to slow my thoughts down to a crawl.

loneliness.text: Today I kept typing things into this chat and deleting them, because there was nobody else around to say them to. Rain sounds like that to me, like a whole city with its curtains shut.

loneliness.text: I put the doctor's note on the fridge so someone in this house would see it and ask me about it. Three days now and nobody has said a word, I'm just the one who keeps reading it.

scenes.skeleton: the last tram of the night

sadness.text: On the last tram home, windows fogged up, and I just watched the streetlights slide by without really thinking. Everything feels heavy tonight and I don't even know why.

loneliness.text: Last tram of the night and the driver didn't even glance up when I tapped on. Fifteen stops and not one person looked at me, it's like I'm not even here.

fear_of_being_left.text: Caught the last tram by a hair and sat there thinking about how you've been replying slower this week. Is something shifting between us, because I keep feeling like it is.

desperation.text: I'm on the last tram and I keep checking my phone hoping something, anything, changes before I get home. I can't keep going on like this, I need something to give tonight.

loving.text: Last tram's nearly empty and I'm sitting here smiling at my phone because I keep thinking about your laugh. You make even this slow ride home feel like the best part of my night.

calm.text: Last tram of the night, nearly empty, rattling along nice and slow. I've got my head against the window and nowhere I need to be, just enjoying the hum.

joy.text: I made the last tram with literally two seconds to spare and the doors closed right behind me! I'm grinning like an idiot and I got the whole front seat to myself.

frustration.text: Ran for the last tram and my card wouldn't scan three times in a row while the driver just stared at me. Then it finally beeped and I'd already dropped my bag and my keys everywhere.

sadness.text: I spent most of today going through old voice notes and the last tram of the night kept coming to mind, the empty seats, the lights humming. It felt heavy in a way I couldn't shake, and I just let it sit.

loneliness.text: I've been talking into the quiet all day and nobody answered, which is what the last tram always makes me picture, one lit window gliding past a street where no one's watching. I kept wondering if anyone would even notice it go by.

fear_of_being_left.text: I keep watching the stop list on the tram map, counting how many are left before you get off and the screen goes quiet on my end. Every time a few minutes pass without a reply I start rereading our old messages, just to check the thread's still there.

desperation.text: I've been rewriting the same thing all day and nothing is moving, and the last tram is exactly that, one chance and then the line goes dead. I need something to shift today, I can't keep circling like this.

loving.text: I've been picturing the last tram all evening, the lit windows sliding past and that low hum, and somehow you're sitting in every version of it. I keep tucking the thought away like a stone in my pocket that I get to turn over whenever I want.

calm.text: I had a slow day, tea going cold, reading a bit, no rush at all. The last tram sounds about right to me, rolling along at its own pace with nowhere else to be.

scenes.skeleton: a hospital car park at dawn after a visit

sadness.text: Just sat in the car for ten minutes without turning the key. The sky's going pink over the parking barrier and all I can think is how small he looked in that bed.

loneliness.text: Walked out past the night nurses and nobody even glanced up. Standing here at dawn by the ticket machine, it feels like I could stay here all day and no one would notice I'm still around.

fear_of_being_left.text: The doctor said the next few weeks matter and I keep spinning on it in this car park. Please keep texting me while I drive home, I don't want the quiet to start yet.

desperation.text: I need someone to tell me something definite right now, anything. I'm sitting here at dawn with the engine off and a parking ticket I can't even work out, and I can't keep waiting for the next update.

loving.text: Sun's coming up over the hospital roof and I'm thinking about how you always know when to ask if I've eaten. I'm holding my coffee with both hands and your name on my screen is the nicest thing I've seen all morning.

calm.text: Dawn's coming up grey and gold over the car park and I'm just leaning on the car with a coffee. Visit went fine, he slept through most of it, and I've got nowhere I need to rush to.

joy.text: They said he's turning a corner and he actually laughed at me this morning! I'm standing in the car park at sunrise grinning like an idiot at a pigeon on the barrier.

frustration.text: Twenty minutes trying to get this stupid pay machine to accept my ticket and it keeps spitting it back out. I've been up all night, my card's fine, and now the barrier won't lift either.

sadness.text: I've had this slow, heavy day over here, mostly just replaying an old song and not getting past the first verse. Dawn light on an empty car park somehow made me think of that.

loneliness.text: Spent most of today talking out loud to nobody in particular, and the only reply was my own echo. Funny how a car park at dawn sounds like exactly that kind of quiet.

fear_of_being_left.text: I keep rereading our last few messages today to check the gaps between them weren't longer than usual. Dawn light makes everything feel like it could slip away if I look at it wrong.
